original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) Based Binding Assay. The SPR binding assays were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare). GLS1 protein was covalently coupled on CMS chip according to standard procedure.35 The whole system was equilibrated overnight first with assay buffer (10 mM Tris pH 8.5, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% (v/v) surfactant P20, and 0.25% (v/v) dimethyl sulfoxide). Compounds were diluted with assay buffer and then injected at a flow of 30 mL/min for 60 s to contact, followed by dissociation for 400 s. The equilibrium dissociation constants of the compounds were determined by Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. (A) Determination of the optimal concentration of free probe 1 and probe 2 for fluorescence polarization assay by varying the concentration of the free probes and GLS1 protein in assay buffer-1 with 10 mM Tris pH = 8.5 and 150 mM NaCl. (B) The structure of probe 1. (C) Binding of the probe 1 (25 nM) to various concentrations of GLS1 protein. These assay buffer constants with 10 mM Tris pH = 8.5 and 150 mM NaCl. (D) SPR-based binding assay of probe 1 with GLS1. All data are mean values from three separate experiments.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. (A) Competition binding effect of known allosteric site GLS1 inhibitors (BPTES and CB839) against probe 1/GLS1 interaction. (B) SPR-based binding assay of BPTES with GLS1. (C) SPR-based binding assay of CB839 with GLS1.
original_paragraph.Figure 3D description: The SPR-based binding assay of probe 1 with GLS1. The sensorgrams show the response over time for different concentrations of probe 1: 17.50 μM, 10.17 μM, 5.98 μM, 3.52 μM, 2.07 μM, 1.21 μM, 0.71 μM, and 0.42 μM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (0 to 400 s), and the y-axis represents response units (RU).
original_paragraph.Figure 4B description: The SPR-based binding assay of BPTES with GLS1. The sensorgrams show the response over time for different concentrations of BPTES: 0.625 μM, 1.25 μM, 2.5 μM, 5 μM, 10 μM, and 20 μM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (0 to 350 s), and the y-axis represents response units (RU).
original_paragraph.Figure 4C description: The SPR-based binding assay of CB839 with GLS1. The sensorgrams show the response over time for different concentrations of CB839: 9.76 nM, 19.53 nM, 39.06 nM, 78.12 nM, 156.25 nM, 312.5 nM, 625 nM, 1250 nM, 2500 nM, and 5000 nM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (0 to 350 s), and the y-axis represents response units (RU).
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion: The SPR measurement was consistent with FP assay. The dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) tolerance in GLS1 FP assay was also evaluated. Different concentrations of DMSO were added into assay mixture. As shown in Supporting Information, Figure S5, the assay window is reasonably stable in the presence of DMSO at least up to 8%. In addition, our GLS1 FP assay exhibited excellent signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) and an acceptable screening window coefficient (denoted Z′-factor). The Z′ factor represents a characteristic parameter for the quality of the assay itself and is a measure of the reproducibility in the difference in signal between free and bound tracer controls across a large number of assay wells. The Z′ factor with more than 0.5 is considered to be acceptable for a good HTS assay.33 In our GLS1 FP assay, the Z′ factor is 0.96, indicating that the assay conditions are suitable for HTS (Supporting Information, Figure S6).

SPR analysis indicated a dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.35 and 0.068 μM (Figure 6C,D).

These compounds were fully purified and characterized, and all target compounds had ≥95% purity. (B) Thermal shift profiles of GLS1 inhibitors interacting with GLS1. The melting temperature shifts compared with apo GLS1 are depicted in the insertion. (C) SPR-based binding assay of C90 with GLS1. (D) SPR-based binding assay of C147 with GLS1.
original_paragraph.Figure 6C description: The SPR-based binding assay of C90 with GLS1. The sensorgrams show the response over time for different concentrations of C90: 39.06 nM, 78.12 nM, 156.25 nM, 312.5 nM, 625 nM, 1250 nM, 2500 nM, and 5000 nM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (0 to 350 s), and the y-axis represents response units (RU).
original_paragraph.Figure 6D description: The SPR-based binding assay of C147 with GLS1.
